## Validation

Primary metrics: MAE on USD and RMSLE on price. Report median absolute percentage error as a secondary scale-free measure, excluding no records merely to improve it. Compare against both baselines with fold-level paired differences. Inspect residuals by hull type, length, age, region, make frequency, and price decile. Calibration plots should compare predicted and observed prices.

## Sensitivity and Robustness

Vary outlier rules, rare-category thresholds, spline complexity, regularization, and retransformation method. Compare pooled versus hull-specific models, random versus grouped folds, and inclusion versus exclusion of detailed location. Bootstrap prediction intervals and model rankings. Report degradation under leave-one-region-out tests.

## Falsification

Reject the preferred model if it fails to beat the hull-median baseline consistently, produces implausible age or length effects, collapses under grouped validation, shows severe regional residual bias, or depends materially on a few extreme listings. Permuted targets must eliminate predictive performance; unexpectedly strong performance would indicate leakage.

## Reviewer Risks

Principal risks are target leakage through category encoding, overfitting rare makes/variants, metric mismatch on a heavy-tailed price distribution, treating advertisements as sales, hidden duplicate listings, and unsupported causal interpretations. The truncated problem excerpt also prevents confirmation of any omitted required subtask.
